transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-20
Start: 15:30 PST
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Evan (Redwood SE), Samir (CTO), Laura (ML Eng), Miguel (Infra), Asha (Product)

Summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Veridian is evaluating embedding strategies for product search + rerank. They are weighting hosting modes due to data residency and throughput SLOs. They want to compare dense 768-dim embeddings vs compact/sparse 128-dim (with post-filtering rerank) for cost and latency and to understand vector DB fanout/backpressure.

--- Transcript body ---
[15:30] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh for setting aside time. quick intros, i'm jordan with redwood, this is priya and evan, our se duo.
[15:35] Samir: yeah thanks, jordan. samir here, cto at veridian. we brought laura and miguel cause this is kinda cross-cutting.
[15:38] Laura: hi all, excited. we mainly want to figure out cost vs recall tradeoffs for our search rerank flow.
[15:45] Jordan: cool, maybe start with a high level of your current flow? what does the pipeline look like today, qps, index sizes, that kinda thing.
[15:50] Miguel: currently we run a dense-sim search using an external vector DB, ~1.1k qps avg during peak, shards across 12 nodes, ~120M docs, embeddings are 768 dims. retention is a problem, some docs have pii and we need to ensure keys never leave our VPC.
[15:55] Priya: ok, good. when you say external DB, is that managed or self-hosted? and which vendor?
[15:58] Miguel: managed right now, using one of the hosted vector services (name redacted), but we're hitting cost and tail latency during promo spikes.
[16:03] Asha: also product wants faster time-to-result in the UI, we can tolerate slight recall loss if rerank with a small LLM can recover. that's why we are exploring smaller dims or sparse representations.
[16:08] Evan: makes sense. high level tradeoff: smaller embeddings reduce fanout and compute on the DB side, but may increase missed candidates which pushes work to the reranker LLM; that can cost on generation tokens.
[16:12] Samir: yeah, we'd love concrete numbers. do you have runbooks or bench numbers for 128 vs 768 dims—both in hosted and dedicated contexts?
[16:16] Priya: we do. at a high level, for Redwood Hosted a 128-dim embedding can cut vector storage and ANN cost by ~3-4x and reduce vector-query latency slightly, but the risk is lower recall and more rerank calls. for Dedicated, we can tune the GPU kernel and KV cache so the latency gap shrinks.
[16:22] Samir: what about sparse embeddings — we've been seeing papers about sparsity preserving recall while shrinking compute.
[16:26] Priya: sparse is promising, but support across vector DBs is uneven. some DBs work better with compressed representations; in practice we've seen 2x compression with small recall loss but integration complexity goes up—padding, custom codecs, and you may need dedicated on-prem infra to control the stack.
[16:32] Miguel: that matters, because we can't have vector data leave our vpc. private deploy or dedicated with VPC peering are the options. can hosted do VPC peering?
[16:36] Jordan: for Hosted we provide endpoint access over TLS and SSO, but for strict VPC isolation you would look at Redwood Dedicated or Private where we can either peer or deploy a private control plane. dedicated offers reserved GPU pools in our cloud region; Private (customer-managed) can be on-prem or in your VPC with KMS integration.
[16:42] Laura: in terms of latency, what's the tail like? our UI needs 95th < 200ms ideally.
[16:46] Priya: with a single-stage ANN (no reranker) at 768 dims, typical 95th on Hosted is ~120-200ms depending on index size and region; under spikes you can see tail spikes unless you have reserved throughput. with a 2-stage flow (128-dim ANN + LLM rerank) you'll see faster first-stage latency but extra time for rerank—if you run the reranker on Dedicated GPUs you can keep end-to-end under 200ms, but cost analysis matters.
[16:54] Samir: pricing—do you charge per token for rerank plus per-embedding for vectors? how do you price dedicated?
[16:59] Jordan: Hosted is usage-based: per-req token + embedding compute + optional embedding storage. Dedicated is committed capacity monthly, so predictable cost; Private is custom license + infra. we'll share a pricing sheet, but rough: heavy rerank token usage usually favors Dedicated if you have steady QPS.
[17:05] Miguel: what about KV cache and prefix caching for rerank? can you keep hot context to avoid repeated LLM runs?
[17:09] Priya: yes, our runtime supports KV cache reuse for repeated prompts and automatic prefix caching which can reduce token generation cost and latency. that's more configurable on Dedicated/Private.
[17:13] Laura: curious about vector DB integration—do you recommend embedding in our existing DB or use Redwood-managed vector indexes?
[17:17] Evan: two paths: 1) keep your DB (we integrate via standard APIs; we also have connectors for Milvus/Pinecone/FAISS), 2) use Redwood's routing to a managed index for initial pilots. For high throughput, sharded index placement matters; if you stick with your DB you may need to add replication for tail headroom.
[17:24] Samir: fanout costs are a hidden surprise for us. when we scale from 100 to 1k qps, fanout multiplies. ideas?
[17:28] Priya: strategies: reduce dims or use hybrid search (metadata filters + smaller embedding probe), increase anisotropy via better model choice, or keep a staged rerank to avoid large final LLM calls for every query. also use local cache for top-K results for frequent queries.
[17:33] Miguel: can Redwood help test different quantization strategies? like 8-bit vs 4-bit or product quantization on the index?
[17:37] Priya: yes, we can recommend quant profiles and test quantized model variants. quantization helps in Dedicated/Private where we can control kernels; for Hosted we have vetted quant profiles. PQ/IVF params are tunable in the index and we can run small experiments to compare recall/latency.
[17:43] Asha: security — we need SOC2, full audit logs, and KMS so customers' keys never leave our control. also, we need contractual data residency in us-west.
[17:48] Jordan: we have SOC2 reports; Dedicated can integrate with customer KMS (bring-your-own-key) and Private can be fully customer-hosted. we'll email SOC2 + network topology diagrams.
[17:52] Samir: what's a realistic pilot path? we want to prove E2E latency under a traffic profile and measure reranker cost tradeoffs.
[17:55] Evan: propose: two-week pilot. week 1: micro-benchmarks — 10k vector index, 128 vs 768 dims, run 1k qps synthetic and capture 50/95/99 latencies and recall. week 2: run a small production slice with real traffic shadowing and measure reranker token spend. SE team will help with data ingestion + index config.
[18:02] Miguel: timeline wise we need security docs before spinning up anything. once we have that, we can give sample data and run the bench.
[18:06] Jordan: sounds good. action items recap — i'll send pricing and contract template; priya/evan will run the bench; miguel sends sample index. schedule follow-up weds 1/28.
[18:09] Laura: quick question — competitors, have you seen other vendors do better on cost?
[18:12] Priya: some vendors make claims on cost but fall short on tail latency and observability. our differentiator is runtime-level batching, automatic caching, and the Dedicated option with SLAs.
[18:16] Samir: ok thanks everyone.
[18:17] Jordan: thanks all. we'll share docs and next steps.

End of transcript.
